producer_author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.content: Conjecture 1.1 is open in this paper; only the graphs treated in the paper are proved to have deterministic limits.
The paper mentions an announced, not-yet-available result of Holmes and Kleptsyn cited as [HK+] and does not use or prove it.
The authors state that each example requires an ad-hoc argument and that proving the conjecture in generality is a difficult open problem. This is an author assessment, not a proved impossibility.
Multiplicity ell of {N,F}: the author asserts it is 'easy to deduce' that other weights vanish and the ell-tuple converges to Dirichlet(1,...,1); no proof is supplied in this paper.
For p=q>=2 the solution of (1.1) is asserted to be alpha=beta=2^{-1/p}; no derivation is given.
The prose explains why the limits of edges 2 and 5 are 1/2 and says the limit 1/2 for edge 3 'seems to be merely a coincidence'. It is informal and not part of the proof.
The passage from system (1.1) to system (1.2) is written with one-line implications; the reverse implication is asserted 'can be obtained similarly' and not expanded.
u*_{a_k}=alpha^k is obtained by 'a straightforward calculation' and the b_l case is called 'similar'; the calculation is not shown.
The second statement of Lemma 6.2 is said to follow 'from similar arguments' and is not written out.
